body: Naruto: The Broken Bond is Ubisoft Montreal's Xbox 360 action-adventure, released in North America on 18 November 2008. It continues Rise of a Ninja through the Search for Tsunade and Sasuke Retrieval story arcs. Exploration and one-on-one combat remain connected, but the sequel adds a tag-team system and a larger playable cast. The player travels through environments designed to feel richer and more densely inhabited, meeting a greater variety of characters between major confrontations. Naruto's developing relationships give the journey its direction as the story moves towards the broken bond of the title.

The tag-team system broadens the combat beyond the abilities of one selected fighter. A larger roster allows different combinations to enter a contest, while adjustments to the fighting system build on the first game's approach. Outside battles, the adventure retains the importance of exploring the environment and moving through the world between story events. Improved lighting and a more painterly visual treatment help distinguish those places. The player alternates between navigating the setting and concentrating on a confrontation, with the available team providing another way to express the relationships already central to the anime.

The sequel replaces the earlier game's borrowed anime scenes with three-dimensional cinematics, keeping story sequences closer to the visual form of the playable adventure. Original anime voices and music maintain another connection to the source. Online competition receives a revised ranking system, while the expanded cast provides more choices for local contests. It was Ubisoft's second and final Naruto game before its licence expired. The Broken Bond develops the earlier adaptation's central attraction: a familiar animated world that can be explored between fights, with the cast and its changing loyalties shaping both parts of the experience.
